blocks.text: An electroplating workshop charges by the gram of silver deposited. The owner does not weigh anything during the job — he sets the current, watches the clock, and knows exactly what he will get. Faraday worked out the arithmetic behind that confidence in the 1830s.

blocks.title: Faraday's two laws
blocks.text: First law: the mass of a substance liberated at an electrode is directly proportional to the quantity of electricity passed through the electrolyte. Second law: when the same quantity of electricity passes through different electrolytes, the masses liberated are proportional to their chemical equivalents.

blocks.caption: Q is charge in coulombs, I is current in amperes and t is time in seconds

blocks.markdown:
## What one faraday means

One **faraday** is the quantity of electricity carried by one mole of electrons, namely 96500 coulombs. That single fact links electricity to the mole and makes every calculation in this topic possible.

Read the half equation to see how many faradays are needed per mole of product.

| Half equation | Electrons per mole | Charge required |
|---|---|---|
| Ag+ + e- -> Ag | 1 | 96500 C for 108 g of silver |
| Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu | 2 | 193000 C for 64 g of copper |
| Al3+ + 3e- -> Al | 3 | 289500 C for 27 g of aluminium |
| 2H+ + 2e- -> H2 | 2 | 193000 C for 22.4 dm3 at s.t.p. |
| 4OH- -> 2H2O + O2 + 4e- | 4 | 386000 C for 22.4 dm3 at s.t.p. |

blocks.title: Time must be in seconds
blocks.text: Q = It only works with time in seconds. Multiply minutes by 60 and hours by 3600 before substituting. A time given as 30 minutes is 1800 s, not 30.

blocks.title: Mass of copper deposited
blocks.prompt: A current of 2.0 A is passed through copper(II) sulphate solution for 30 minutes using copper electrodes. Calculate the mass of copper deposited at the cathode. [Cu = 64, 1 faraday = 96500 C]

steps.text: Convert the time to seconds: 30 x 60 = 1800 s.
Find the quantity of electricity passed.
Write the cathode half equation: Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu. Two moles of electrons deposit one mole of copper.
So 2 x 96500 = 193000 C deposits 64 g of copper.
Set up the proportion for 3600 C.
Check the scale: 3600 C is roughly one fiftieth of 193000 C, and 64 divided by 50 is about 1.3, which is close to our answer.

blocks.answer: About 1.19 g of copper is deposited

blocks.title: Volume of gas liberated
blocks.prompt: Calculate the volume of oxygen, measured at s.t.p., liberated at the anode when 9650 C of electricity is passed through acidified water. [1 faraday = 96500 C; molar volume = 22.4 dm3]

steps.text: Write the anode half equation: 4OH- -> 2H2O + O2 + 4e-. Four moles of electrons release one mole of oxygen.
So the charge needed for one mole of oxygen is 4 x 96500 = 386000 C.
Find the moles of oxygen liberated by 9650 C.
Convert moles to volume at s.t.p.
As a cross-check, 9650 C is exactly 0.1 faraday, that is 0.1 mol of electrons, and one quarter of that is 0.025 mol of oxygen. The two routes agree.

Electrolytic refining of copper to the 99.99 percent purity needed for electrical cable
Extraction of aluminium from purified bauxite dissolved in molten cryolite
Manufacture of chlorine, hydrogen and sodium hydroxide from brine
Anodising aluminium to thicken its protective oxide layer

blocks.title: Always start from the half equation
blocks.text: The number of electrons in the half equation is what turns coulombs into grams. Write it down first, every time. Forgetting the factor of 2 for Cu2+ or 3 for Al3+ is the single largest source of lost marks in this topic.

points: Quantity of electricity Q equals current in amperes multiplied by time in seconds.
One faraday, 96500 C, is the charge carried by one mole of electrons.
The half equation gives the number of faradays needed per mole of product.
Mass liberated is proportional to the charge passed, which is Faraday's first law.
For the same charge, masses liberated in different cells are proportional to their chemical equivalents.
Electrolysis underpins electroplating, copper refining and the extraction of aluminium.
